estorage-import-hint: An empty filter takes everything. Otherwise only the listed types.
estorage-export-hint: Pushes only filter types into the facing inventory.
estorage-storage-hint: The facing chest shows in the terminal. An empty filter shows everything.
estorage-interface-hint: The top row places items into the machine. The middle row holds patterns. The bottom row sets what to keep; the sample is not consumed.
block-handbooktext-estoragechest: One disk and a terminal. Sneak to insert or remove the disk. A normal click opens the network.
block-handbooktext-estoragemonitor: Shows the network craft queue. Cancel clears it.
block-handbooktext-estorageemitter: Compares how many of an item are in the network with a threshold. An import or export bus beside it runs only while the emitter is on.
block-handbooktext-estoragewireless: The wireless terminal opens the network within 32 blocks while this block has a channel and the controller has power.
block-handbooktext-estoragep2p: Sneak cycles frequency 1–8. Two blocks on the same frequency: the input uses 1 channel and the output provides 32 more.
estorage-assembler-hint: The interface puts a pattern's ingredients here. The craft finishes on its own and the result returns to the network.
estorage-assembler-idle: Waiting for a pattern from the interface
estorage-craft-tool: Recipes with a tool or a returned item are not supported yet
estorage-pattern-hint: The grid matches the inventory workbench. The blank pattern sits on the right, and the button puts the encoded pattern in the second slot.
estorage-pattern-blank: Blank. Encode a recipe in the pattern terminal.
estorage-pattern-noblank: Put a blank pattern in the left slot beside the grid
estorage-pattern-outputfull: The second slot has no room for a different pattern
estorage-pattern-craft-tip: Crafting: the workbench grid and one output cell from the recipe
estorage-pattern-process-tip: Processing: three output cells to the right of the grid. No grid recipe is required
estorage-pattern-substitute-tip: Substitution: the pattern is marked so similar items can stand in
estorage-pattern-out: The encoded pattern comes out here
estorage-pattern-needout: Put a product in the processing output cells
estorage-bus-nolink: No inventory on the facing side
estorage-nopower: No power. Connect the controller to a 128 V line
estorage-nocontroller: No controller. Link the blocks with network cable
estorage-conflict: Two controllers are on the same network
estorage-disk-hint: Insert into a drive. Items are accessed from a terminal.
estorage-cell-hint: Insert into a drive. Liquid is accessed from the liquid terminal.
block-handbooktext-estoragecontroller: Heart of the network. Controllers that share a face are one multiblock: each block adds 32 channels. A second controller reached only by cable breaks the network. A cable strand passes 8, and four strands pass 32. One 128 V connection powers the whole network. Draw is paid once: 8 W idle, plus 10 W per drive, 6 W per terminal, 4 W per bus, 6 W per interface, 8 W per assembler and 2 W per inserted disk or cell.
block-handbooktext-estoragecable: Sits on a solid face, the same way an electrical wire does. Another click adds a segment; breaking removes the segment under the cursor. It does not carry electricity. Clicking a segment that is already there adds a strand, up to four. One strand passes 8 channels per controller, and each extra strand adds 8. Each device uses one.
block-handbooktext-estoragedrive: Eight slots for disks and liquid cells. Items are taken from the terminal, liquid from the liquid terminal. A removed disk or cell keeps its contents.
block-handbooktext-estorageterminal: Attaches to a solid face, like an electric lamp: floor, wall, or ceiling. Access every disk on the network while the controller has power. Left click takes a stack, right click takes one. Shift moves items between the terminal and your inventory.
block-handbooktext-estorageliquidtermina: Mounts the same way as the item terminal. Shows liquid stored on cells in the drives. A bucket, bowl, or jug pours the whole stack on left click and one litre from a single container on right click. An empty stack on a slot fills every container, and right click fills one litre into one container. A liquid portion can also be moved like an item. One cell holds up to four liquids and they share the litres: 1k stores 8192 litres, and each tier holds four times more.
block-handbooktext-estorageimport: Place it against a chest or machine, on the face you click. While the controller has power it pulls items into the network. Right click opens the filter: empty takes everything, otherwise only the sample types. Samples are not consumed.
block-handbooktext-estorageexport: Place it against a chest or machine, on the face you click. It pushes network items that match the filter. With an empty filter it pushes nothing. Samples are not consumed.
block-handbooktext-estoragestorage: Place it against a chest, on the face you click. While the controller has power that chest is visible in the terminal and can be withdrawn from there. New deposits fill disks first; the overflow goes into the chest. An empty filter allows every type, otherwise only the samples.
block-handbooktext-estorageinterface: Mounts like the terminal, including on a quern. Three rows. The top row places items into the input of the block it is mounted on. The middle row holds encoded patterns. The bottom row sets what to place and how many: the sample is not consumed, and the network fills the top row. The item terminal shows a slot with the pattern result. Click it, choose a quantity, and press Order: that interface feeds the pattern ingredients into the input and pulls the output until the order is filled. One channel, 6 W.
block-handbooktext-estorageassembler: Place it flush against an interface. It does not store the recipe: the interface fills its grid with the pattern's ingredients, then the assembler consumes them and returns the result to the network. Several assemblers around one interface work at the same time.
block-handbooktext-estoragepatterntermin: Mounts like the item terminal and shows the network. The bottom is a workbench grid: crafting has one recipe output, processing has three. The recipe output sits to the right of the grid. Along the bottom: a blank pattern, a right arrow, and the finished pattern. Items in the grid are not consumed. Substitution marks the pattern.
block-handbooktext-estoragestock: Put a sample in the slot. Shows how many of that item are in the network. Take and sneak give one stack. Craft orders a stack when a pattern exists.
estorage-cell-hint: Left click takes a stack, right click takes one.
